subject.title: Cron jobs stall during AI model calls (model_call:stream_progress never completes)

question: Should this issue remain the canonical tracker for cron `wake` mode `now` result semantics now that the isolated model-stream stall is fixed on main, or should maintainers split that remaining bug into a new focused issue and close this as implemented after release verification?
rationale: The code evidence is strong for both the main-only headline fix and the remaining fire-and-forget wake contract gap, but deciding whether to keep a broad external report open or split it is a maintainer tracking/product decision.

options.title: Split wake contract tracker
options.body: Create or designate a narrow cron wake-now result issue, carry over the source evidence, and close this issue once the main-only stream-stall fix is release-verified.

options.title: Keep this as canonical
options.body: Retitle and scope this issue to cron wake-now result semantics, accepting that the original stream-progress title is now misleading.

options.title: Close after next-release retest
options.body: Treat Bug 3 as too separate for this report and ask for a fresh issue only if users can still reproduce wake-now mismatch after the next release.

recommendation.title: Split wake contract tracker
recommendation.body: Create or designate a narrow cron wake-now result issue, carry over the source evidence, and close this issue once the main-only stream-stall fix is release-verified.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus authored the current scoping comment and the merged run-lifecycle stack that changed the status of the headline bug.
